name: {ai} engineering
_note: Single source of truth for the {ai} engineering visual system. Every colour, type step, radius, shadow and motion value used by the CLI, docs/blueprint.html and the ai-engineering-web landing site is declared here or derived from here by scripts/brand.ts. Nothing downstream may invent a value.

provenance.excluded: nothing: every family LeafyGreen publishes is copied, because the artifact syntax highlighter uses purple and yellow as code colours.
provenance.trademark: No MongoDB logo, wordmark, leaf glyph or brand asset is reproduced anywhere. This system adopts the palette, the type treatment, the geometry and the component shapes — the visual grammar, not the identity.

bg-mid.purpose: Alternating band backgrounds and raised tints.

surface-2.purpose: Terminal window bodies, code wells, stat tiles.

surface-ivory.purpose: The one light surface: emphasis panels that must break the dark field, exactly as mongodb.com does.

surface-3.purpose: Opaque raised surface, for artifacts that must render standalone with no compositing.

border.purpose: 1px component borders. Neutral, and bright enough to be safe: this token is used for both decorative edges and control boundaries, so it must clear 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11) on EVERY surface it can sit on, not just the field — gray.dark1 measured 3.16:1 on the field but only 2.76:1 on a raised surface, which is a control nobody can see. Decorative dividers use `hairline` instead.

hairline.purpose: Dividers and window separators — decorative, so the 3:1 rule does not bind them.

muted-dim.purpose: Decorative and disabled text only — never load-bearing prose.

on-accent.purpose: Text sitting on a green fill.

on-ivory-muted.purpose: Secondary text on the ivory surface.

accent.purpose: The one signal colour: primary fills, borders, focus, large UI, terminal tags.

accent-text.purpose: Small inline and heading green. Never set body-size green to the vivid base — it buzzes.

accent-deep.purpose: Tinted washes and hover fills behind green text.

link.purpose: Links, list bullets and directional arrows — the second, quieter voice.

focus.purpose: Focus rings. Blue, so focus never reads as brand emphasis.

danger.purpose: The one state that blocks — lifted to red.light1 so it survives on the dark field.

artifact._note: The HTML artifacts ai-engineering generates (a brainstorm, a research page, a recap, the checkpoint viewer) must render standalone with no request of their own, so their token block is INLINED — which is exactly how one palette becomes three. This map is a second set of NAMES for these values, never a second set of values: `bun scripts/brand.ts artifact` reads the files that carry the block and fails if any of them disagrees with what is written here, and tests/artifact-brand.spec.ts fails the build on that gate.
artifact.ungated: --mono and --sans in the artifact block are NOT gated: an artifact may be opened from a folder with no network and no installed webfont, so it names system font stacks instead of the brand's. That is a deliberate difference between the site and the artifacts, not drift.

typography.substitution_note: MongoDB's own faces (Euclid Circular A, and the condensed display grotesque on mongodb.com) are commercial and are NOT shipped. Archivo is the open substitute: one variable family that covers both the normal-width UI voice and, via its width axis, the heavy condensed display voice. JetBrains Mono stays for code, terminal output and the instrumented labels. The substitution is stated in DESIGN.md, not hidden.

lit-edge.purpose: Top-edge highlight. Neutral light now, not a brand tint.

window.purpose: Floats windows and cards off the field.

card.purpose: Card hover lift only; flat at rest.

glow.purpose: The one brand halo, behind the hero and on primary-button hover.

cli._note: The terminal cannot be trusted with a background colour — the user's terminal owns it. So the CLI never paints prose in brand green: the banner frame and braces carry the brand, the wordmark stays at the terminal's default foreground (legible on a light terminal and a dark one alike), and status marks keep the terminal's own named ANSI colours, which every theme already tunes for legibility.
